commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Coco
commitResults.messageBody:
Renamed Duke.java to Coco.java, updated the class name and ASCII
banner, and updated README.md and docs/README.md to reference the
new name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark command to update list status
Add unmark command to update status of list
Change to use task class for implementation
Add delete feature and update testing
Add save and load of tasks to disk
commitResults.messageBody:
Persist the task list to ./data/coco.txt (relative, OS-independent path)
so it survives across runs. Storage.load() rebuilds tasks on startup and
returns an empty list on first run when the file/folder doesn't exist
yet; Storage.save() is called after every mutation (add/mark/unmark/
delete) and creates the data folder if needed. Malformed lines in a
hand-edited data file are skipped instead of crashing the program.

Also update run_ui_tests.py to wipe data/ before each test case, since
persistence would otherwise leak task state between the UI test plan's
supposedly-independent test cases.

Deadline now stores its /by date as a java.time.LocalDate instead of a
free-text String. Input must be yyyy-mm-dd (e.g. 2019-10-15); an
unparseable date now gets the same kind of CocoException as a missing
one, instead of being accepted as arbitrary text. Display formats it as
MMM dd yyyy (e.g. Oct 15 2019). Storage round-trips it via LocalDate's
default ISO-8601 toString(), and skips a saved deadline line whose date
fails to parse, consistent with how other malformed lines are handled.

Event's /from and /to stay free-text strings, per the increment's
minimal scope.

Updated the UI test plan: existing deadline test cases used free-text
dates ("Sunday", "June 6th") that are no longer valid input, so they're
swapped for yyyy-mm-dd dates with the new formatted output (re-captured
by actually running the program, not hand-typed). Test 6 also gained a
case for a /by value that isn't a valid date.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui, Storage, Parser, TaskList classes for better OOP
commitResults.messageBody:
Coco.java previously mixed console I/O, argument parsing, task-list
mutation, and persistence directly in one big switch statement. Split
those concerns into four classes per the increment's minimal target:

- Ui: all System.out printing and Scanner-based input reading.
- Storage: unchanged load/save logic, but now instance-based
  (constructed with the data file path) instead of static, so Coco
  owns one Storage instance rather than calling static methods.
- Parser: the command-word dispatch (delegates to the existing Command
  enum) plus all the argument-parsing/validation that used to live
  inline in each switch case (todo/deadline/event field extraction,
  deadline date parsing, task-index parsing).
- TaskList: wraps the List<Task> and its add/remove/get/size
  operations.

Coco itself is now a thin orchestrator: an instance holding one Ui,
Storage, and TaskList, with a run() method that dispatches parsed
commands to them. This is a pure refactor - no behavior or output
changed (all 11 UI test cases pass unchanged, byte-for-byte).

Task/Todo/Deadline/Event/CocoException/Command are unchanged; they
already modeled a single, cohesive responsibility each.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into the coco package
commitResults.messageBody:
Minimal target for this increment: put all classes in one package.
Moved every class from src/main/java/*.java into src/main/java/coco/
and added the package coco; declaration to each. src/main/java stays
the source root, per the project's tooling conventions.

The main class is now coco.Coco, so:
- README's IDE setup instructions point at the new file location.
- test-ui's run_ui_tests.py compiles recursively (rglob) instead of a
  flat glob, since sources now live under a package subdirectory, and
  its default main class is coco.Coco.

No behavior change - all 11 UI test cases still pass unchanged.

The Gradle scaffold from add-gradle-support was written for the
original seedu.duke.Duke class/package name and duke.jar output
filename. Update both to match this project's actual main class
(coco.Coco, from the A-Packages increment) and jar name (coco.jar).

Verified: `./gradlew build` succeeds, `./gradlew run` correctly reads
piped stdin (the run.standardInput = System.in config from the
scaffold), and `java -jar build/libs/coco.jar` runs the chatbot
correctly. The plain javac-based test-ui skill still passes all 11
cases unchanged, so both build paths work side by side.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for Parser and Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Minimal target for this increment: at least two non-trivial methods
from two different classes, tested reasonably well.

Parser is the most logic-heavy class (all the command validation that
used to live inline in Coco's switch statement), so it gets the most
coverage: parseTodo, parseDeadline, parseEvent, and parseIndex, each
with its happy path plus every rejection branch (missing markers,
empty fields, non-numeric/out-of-range indices, unparseable dates).

Storage gets tests for the load()/save() round trip across all three
task types and done-status, the missing-file and missing-parent-folder
cases from Level 7, and the corrupted-line handling from Level 8
(unknown type letter, too few fields, unparseable date) - each
asserting that only the bad line is skipped and good ones still load.
Storage's constructor already takes the data file path as a String
(from A-MoreOOP), so tests point it at a JUnit @TempDir instead of the
real ./data folder.

Run via `./gradlew test`; all 23 tests pass. Verified the plain
javac-based test-ui skill is unaffected (only compiles src/main/java).

commitResults.messageTitle: Document building and running the executable JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
The shadowJar task was already configured correctly by A-Gradle
(archiveFileName = 'coco.jar', mainClass = 'coco.Coco'), so this
increment is mostly verification: confirmed the exact grading workflow
works - copy build/libs/coco.jar into an empty folder, run
`java -jar "coco.jar"` from there, and the chatbot starts, creates
./data/coco.txt relative to that folder, and correctly reloads saved
tasks (including their done status) on a second run from the same
folder.

Added a short README section documenting the gradlew run/test/
shadowJar commands, since the project previously only documented the
IntelliJ-based workflow.

Per the increment's instructions, the built JAR itself is not
committed here; it should be attached to a GitHub release instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaDoc comments to all classes and public methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Covers every class in the coco package (Stretch goal target: all
non-private classes and methods, plus the non-trivial private helpers
Storage.parseLine and Parser.argumentsOf). Follows the SE-EDU Java
coding standard's JavaDoc conventions: summary-first sentence, blank
line before @param/@return, "Returns..." phrasing for accessor
methods, and single-line /** ... */ form for trivial one-liners.

Per that same standard, overridden methods (toString/toSaveFormat)
keep just @Override with no repeated JavaDoc, since the standard
explicitly allows omitting it when the parent's doc already applies.
Protected fields and enum constants are also left uncommented, since
the increment's scope is specifically classes and methods.

Pure documentation change - no behavior touched. All 11 UI test cases
and all 23 JUnit tests still pass, and `javadoc` itself only emits
info-level "no comment"/"no @return" warnings for the
fields/constants/default-constructor that are outside this increment's
scope - no errors.

This project didn't yet document or enforce a specific coding
standard, so style was whatever felt reasonable at the time. Adopt
the SE-EDU intermediate Java standard and Git conventions as the
project's standard going forward, so future contributions (human or
AI) stay consistent.

Two new project skills capture the rules so they get applied
automatically rather than re-derived each time:
- seedu-java-coding-standard: naming, layout, imports, JavaDoc.
- seedu-git-standard: commit message and branch name conventions.

AGENTS.md now points at both and says to apply them without being
asked.

Auditing the existing code against the standard found it already
compliant almost everywhere (4-space indent, K&R braces, explicit
imports, no wildcard imports, always-braced conditionals, etc.). The
one fix: Parser.parseIndex's wrapped ternary is now in the standard's
three-line form (condition, then "? value", then ": value", each on
its own line) instead of cramming the false branch onto the same line
as the true branch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Give users a way to find a task without scrolling through the whole
list: `find <keyword>` matches tasks whose description contains the
keyword (case-insensitively) and prints just those, renumbered from 1,
under a "Here are the matching tasks in your list:" header - mirroring
`list`'s format but scoped to the matches, per the increment's example.

- Command gets a new FIND value.
- Parser.parseFind extracts and validates the keyword (same
  empty-argument rejection pattern as the other parse* methods).
- TaskList.find does the case-insensitive substring match over each
  task's description, returning matches in original list order.
- Ui.showFindResults prints them; Coco wires FIND to it.

Added parseFind and TaskList.find unit tests (happy path, no matches,
empty list, case-insensitivity) alongside the existing Parser/Storage
tests. Added Test 12 to the UI test plan, output captured by actually
running the program.

branch-Level-9 (the find command) was built in parallel with
branch-A-JavaDoc and branch-A-CodingStandard, off the same base commit,
per this increment's instructions - so it doesn't yet have JavaDoc or
the coding-standard fixes those branches added to master in the
meantime.

Conflict in Parser.java: both sides inserted new content at the same
spot, right before parseIndex. master (via A-JavaDoc) had added
parseIndex's doc comment there; branch-Level-9 had added the whole new
parseFind method there. Resolved by keeping both - parseFind first
(matching command declaration order in Command.java), then parseIndex's
doc comment and signature - and gave parseFind matching JavaDoc so it
reads consistently with the rest of the now-documented file.

Coco.java, Command.java, TaskList.java, and Ui.java all merged
automatically (their find-related additions landed in different spots
than the JavaDoc/style changes), but Ui.showFindResults and
TaskList.find came from the pre-JavaDoc branch without doc comments;
added matching ones for consistency with their now fully-documented
files - `javadoc` was re-run afterward to confirm no gaps remained
beyond the pre-existing, already-accepted omissions (enum constants,
protected fields, trivial one-line getters).

Re-ran the full check after resolving: `./gradlew build` (30 JUnit
tests) and the test-ui skill (12 UI test cases) both pass.
